technical_and_design_decisions: All implementation will target Java 17+ and Spring Framework 6.0+ as per the framework's current requirements.
For reliable HDFS writes (U2), the HDFS sync() API will be used to confirm data is persisted to disk before sending an acknowledgement to the message bus, with retry logic for failed commits.

For partition function override (U3), a strategy pattern will be used, with a new PartitionStrategy interface that users can implement and configure via module properties to override the default partitioner.

For multi topic-partition consumption (U4), the existing Kafka consumer will be extended to support multiple topic-partition assignments per instance, with a thread-safe blocking queue used to aggregate messages from all assigned partitions into a single consumer queue.

For the Flo DSL parser (U5), a context registry will be added to the parser to store previously parsed stream definitions, enabling validation of cross-stream references and module/option values against existing stream context.

For single container stream deployment (U6), Docker will be used for containerization, with a shared Docker network and shared volumes for inter-module communication and data persistence, respectively.

For non-default ConfigurableConversionService tuples (U7), custom Jackson deserialization logic will be added for ConfigurableConversionService beans to preserve non-default converter configurations during deserialization.

For JMX benchmarking (U8), JMH (Java Microbenchmark Harness) will be used for isolated performance testing, with test scenarios covering both JMX enabled and disabled states, measuring throughput and end-to-end latency.

The Flo UI development team will provide required integration points and sample UI payloads for the new DSL parser (U5) within the development timeline.
A dedicated test environment with JMX monitoring tools is available for running the JMX benchmarks required for U8.
All changes implemented for this increment will maintain backward compatibility with existing public APIs, so no additional migration guides or deprecation work is required.
The project's existing code review and merge process will be handled by other team members, so no effort is allocated for those activities.
